content.text:
Three endpoints require `ManageUsers`, all on the `User` aggregate root:

- `POST /users` (add)
- `PUT /users/{id}` (update)
- `DELETE /users/{id}` (remove)

`GET /users` and `GET /users/{id}` only require an authenticated user.

**Where the requirement is set and enforced**
- **Model:** `specs/aggregates.yaml:37-41` sets `mandatory_right: ManageUsers` on `add`, `update` and `remove`.
- **Generated endpoints:** `src/UM.Api/UMEndpoints.g.cs:54,61,68` attaches `.RequireRight("ManageUsers")` to each of those routes.
- **Enforcement:** `RequireRight` in `src/UM.Api/Framework/Security.f.cs:26` turns this into an authorization policy named `right:ManageUsers`. The `RightPolicyProvider` in the same file builds that policy on demand. It requires an authenticated user who holds the `ManageUsers` claim or `*`. A caller without it gets a 401 or 403 before the handler runs.

I only read the `RequireRight` helper. I didn't read the body of `RightPolicyProvider`, so the claim and `*` check comes from its doc comment and `AGENTS.md`.
